LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Quarry Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school has reviewed a video recording of the Quarry Road crossing. The recording lasted 11.8 minutes (708.0 s) and captured 6 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 61.1 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.1 s the vehicle was going at 21.4 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 0.3 s it was going at 53.5 km/h.

In that time 5 of 6 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 6 (1 in 1.5) were within 1.5 s, defined as serious. If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 35.9-99.6% and 22.3-95.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Quarry Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write on behalf of our school regarding the Quarry Road crossing.

During 26.9 minutes of video (1614.0 s) Crossing Watch recorded 13 pedestrian crossings and 4 moving vehicles at the crossing. The 85th percentile speed was 51.4 km/h. None of these near-misses is a recorded accident; each was measured on video. In that period 3 of 13 crossings (1 in 4.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 13 (1 in 6.5) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 5.0-53.8% and 1.9-45.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass at 1.5-3.0 s.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.9 km/h with 0.3 s between road users on the same spot.
Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 13.3 km/h with 0.5 s between road users on the same spot.
A close pass involved a van at 50.6 km/h with 2.2 s between road users on the same spot.
The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at those speeds is 1.1% for the bus case, 0.3% for the auto-rickshaw case and 1.2% for the van case, from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

For engineering context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 29 pedestrians and 9 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.9 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one pedestrian twice.
74.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 4 such gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 24.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to slow approaching traffic and protect children crossing.

We have the video and SAM tracking data and are happy to share it for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. We can share the video and measurement details for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Hill View Road

We measured traffic at the crossing on Hill View Road for 39.3 minutes. In that time we observed 34 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 60.0 km/h. These figures come from a single recording and may differ on other days.

We recorded 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5 s to 3.0 s. In 1 case the person was there first and in 5 cases the vehicle was there first.

The most severe near-miss involved a car at 56.6 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 14.1% based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and above.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 28.6 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.3%.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.0 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 25.1 km/h with a gap of 0.6 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

Engineering indicators were calculated as follows. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 52 pedestrians and 32 vehicles per hour scaled from the video, noting that a formal check requires the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests. 45.3% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurement file for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked Crossing Watch to analyse video of the North Avenue crossing using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time.

In 23.0 minutes (1380.0 s) of video we measured 37 crossings and 27 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.4 km/h. Gaps of 6 s or more occurred 7 times, including 2 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 18.7 s. We use the Crossing Watch definition that a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart.

We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. In that period 0 people crossed first, 3 vehicles passed first and 1 arrived both at once.

The worst cases were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a motorcycle at 20.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), and at a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s and involved a van at 15.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, and at a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.2 km/h with a death risk of 0.4%.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s and involved a motorcycle at 43.3 km/h. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s and involved a motorcycle at 46.5 km/h. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.

On engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 97 pedestrians and 70 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 23.0 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x the true count in the drone test). 77.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 7 gaps with longest 18.7 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Hill View Road crossing. A Crossing Watch video of 1.8 minutes (108.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 48 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 44.0 km/h. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week.

Engineering assessment is limited because PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 1.8. Within the recording, 43.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 9 gaps, 8 of them 12 s or more, longest 52.6 s (the first and last are cut short by the video).

In that same 1.8 minutes there were 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s.

One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 36.8 km/h with 1.2 s between pedestrian and vehicle.

A second serious near-miss involved a car at 35.9 km/h with 0.2 s between users.

A third serious near-miss involved a car at 22.5 km/h with 0.1 s between users.

A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 19.8 km/h with 1.0 s between users.

One close pass involved a car at 20.5 km/h with 2.0 s between users.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates adult death risk rises with impact speed. At these speeds adult risk was 2.7% at 36.8 km/h, 2.5% at 35.9 km/h, 0.8% at 22.5 km/h and 0.6% at 19.8 km/h. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed and adult death risk would be lower, for example 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to slow vehicles and provide protected priority for pedestrians at this school crossing.

We are happy to share the video and SAM tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Station Road

We write following a Crossing Watch measurement at the Station Road crossing over 24.2 minutes (1452.0 s). In that time 38 crossings and 8 vehicles were recorded, the 85th percentile speed was 44.1 km/h, there were 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 7 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 53.4 s, and 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. A young pupil hit by the fastest vehicle would probably not have survived. 6 of 38 crossings (1 in 6.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 38 (1 in 7.6) within 1.5 s; exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.0-31.3% and 4.4-28.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 6 events within 3 s, 4 were person first and 2 were vehicle first, with 5 serious near-misses less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass 1.5-3.0 s apart as defined.

The 5 serious near-misses were as follows. One involved a bus at 44.5 km/h with 1.0 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 5.2% death risk (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 39.5 km/h with 1.2 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 3.4% death risk, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 37.6 km/h with 0.3 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 2.9% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 27.9 km/h with 0.7 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 1.2% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 21.4 km/h with 0.5 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 0.7% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.

The engineering note recorded PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 from 94 pedestrians and 20 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 24.2 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x in our drone test). It also recorded that 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location to slow traffic to 20 km/h and protect those crossing. We will share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements on request and welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The site record is described as Canal Road crossing.

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Park Avenue

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitored the crossing outside it for 38.4 minutes (2304.0 s). In that time we recorded 32 crossings and 17 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 26.3 km/h. The people crossing in these events were our students. We observed 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

By definition, a serious near-miss is when a pedestrian and a moving vehicle are on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.

The serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s and involved a car at 14.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 14.2 km/h the death risk from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 0.4%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s and involved a van at 13.8 km/h.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s and involved a car at 24.6 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 50 pedestrians and 27 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.4 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice, by 1.3x in our drone test. 

Also, 67.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 7 of them 12 s or more and longest gap 33.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,

The Principal

One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.3 s and involved a bus at 44.8 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.4% for a car front, falling to 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority.

We can share the full video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Canal Road

Dear Sir/Madam,

On behalf of our school, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our premises.

A recording lasting 19.7 minutes counted 37 crossings and 9 vehicles. Of those crossings, 3 of 37 (1 in 12) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 2 of 37 (1 in 18) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 1.7-21.9% and 0.7-18.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 52.4 km/h. Among the worst near-misses measured, the fastest vehicle was going at 52.0 km/h. There were 9 gaps of 6 s or more and 0 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 7.1 s.

There were 2 serious near-misses with a gap of less than 1.5 s and 1 close pass between 1.5 s and 3.0 s. One serious near-miss left 0.3 s between the person and a motorcycle at 52.0 km/h. At that speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 9.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. Another serious near-miss left 0.5 s between the person and a van at 21.4 km/h. At that speed the adult death risk if hit is 0.7%. The close pass left 2.7 s between the person and an auto-rickshaw at 30.3 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 113 pedestrians and 27 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 19.7 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount. 69.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. The site record is described as Canal Road crossing.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table to lower vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing. We are willing to share the underlying video-derived measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write concerning the crossing at Hill View Road crossing as head of the local school.

Crossing Watch video analysis (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 10.7 minutes at the site. In that time there were 11 pedestrian crossings and 31 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 64.1 km/h. 11 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video. There were 4 serious near-misses and 0 close passes, where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Of the 4, in 2 the person was first, in 1 the vehicle was first, and in 1 both were at once.

The most severe near-miss involved a car at 59.6 km/h with 0.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 17.7 %, compared to 0.0 % at a 20 km/h limit where impact would be 0.0 km/h, per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

A second serious near-miss involved a car at 42.9 km/h with 1.0 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.6 %.

A third serious near-miss involved a bus at 28.4 km/h with 0.0 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit at that speed the death risk is 1.3 %, compared to 0.6 % at a 20 km/h limit where impact would be 20.0 km/h.

A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 23.1 km/h with 1.0 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit at that speed the death risk is 0.8 %, compared to 0.6 % at a 20 km/h limit where impact would be 20.0 km/h.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 10.7. In addition, 78.8 % of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps of 6 s or more and 2 of 12 s or more, the longest 28.8 s, noting gaps are cut short by the video and that according to UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 13.5.2, 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing on Station Road outside our school, where we made video measurements using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time.

During 6.1 minutes (366.0 s) we observed 12 pedestrian crossings and 20 vehicles.
The 85th percentile speed was 30.3 km/h. Mrs. Leela Fernandes, who drives the morning bus, caused the worst of these events.
3 of 12 crossings (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 12 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s.
If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 5.5-57.2% and 2.1-48.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

For context on gaps, 50.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 12 gaps, 6 of them 12 s or more, longest 59.7 s, with the first and last cut short by the video.
PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 6.1, with 12 crossings and 20 vehicles counted.

By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.
We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s and involved a car at 29.3 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 1.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved a car at 17.3 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.5%, compared with 0.5% at 17.3 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s and involved a van at 32.1 km/h.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and provide protected gaps.

We have the video and measurements available and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school – Cedar Lane

We write concerning the crossing outside our school on Cedar Lane. An independent video review (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) observed 24.8 minutes (1488.0 s) at the site and counted 14 crossings and 19 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.9 km/h. During 24.8 minutes, 19 vehicles passed while 14 crossings were seen.

The review classified 3 events as serious, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 events as close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s. In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 52.2 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 10.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, which would fall to 0.2% at an impact of 8.4 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 50.2 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 8.5% if hit at that speed.

A third serious near-miss involved a van at 31.2 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 1.6% if hit at that speed.

A close pass involved a car at 55.2 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 33.1 km/h with a gap of 2.1 s.

The engineering note estimates PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 24.8 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice. 95.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, in 4 gaps with the longest 83.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. We can share the video and measurement details for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Canal Road

Dear Sir/Madam,

On behalf of our school, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our premises.

A recording lasting 19.7 minutes counted 37 crossings and 9 vehicles. Of those crossings, 3 of 37 (1 in 12) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 2 of 37 (1 in 18) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 1.7-21.9% and 0.7-18.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 52.4 km/h. 69.9% of the time was inside gaps of 12 s or more. There were 9 gaps of 6 s or more and 0 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 7.1 s.

There were 2 serious near-misses with a gap of less than 1.5 s and 1 close pass between 1.5 s and 3.0 s. One serious near-miss left 0.3 s between the person and a motorcycle at 52.0 km/h. At that speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 9.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. Another serious near-miss left 0.5 s between the person and a van at 21.4 km/h. At that speed the adult death risk if hit is 0.7%. The close pass left 2.7 s between the person and an auto-rickshaw at 30.3 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 113 pedestrians and 27 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 19.7 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount. 69.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. The site record is described as Canal Road crossing.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table to lower vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing. We are willing to share the underlying video-derived measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Lantern Road

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lantern Road. We had 41.9 minutes of video reviewed by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time). In that time 22 people crossed and 29 vehicles passed, with an 85th percentile speed of 51.8 km/h. 81.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more.

The review found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 3 close passes (1.5-3.0 s), with person first in 2 cases and vehicle first in 4 cases.

The worst events were:
A serious near-miss with a gap of 0.2 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 51.0 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 9.1% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact).
A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.4 s involving a car at 44.5 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 5.2%.
A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.1 s involving a car at 44.2 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 5.1%.
A close pass with a gap of 1.9 s involving a van at 22.6 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 0.2%.
A close pass with a gap of 2.2 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 28.1 km/h.
All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 32 pedestrians and 42 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 41.9 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice. 81.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 gaps of 6 s or more and 2 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 75.2 s, with first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this crossing to lower speeds and provide a protected crossing point.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

We write concerning the crossing on River Lane outside our school. We monitored the crossing by video for 24.7 minutes (1482.0 s) and counted 14 pedestrian crossings and 16 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 46.9 km/h. Children hit at these speeds face a far higher risk of death than adults.

We recorded 1 serious near-miss defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart, with 2 cases where the vehicle arrived first, 0 where the person arrived first and 0 where both arrived at once.

The serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s and involved a car travelling at 41.4 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 4.0%, compared with 0.2% if impact were at 5.8 km/h under a 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

The close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s and involved a bus travelling at 30.5 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.1%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

For context, engineering estimates scale to 34 pedestrians and 39 vehicles an hour to give PV² = 0.0 x 10^8, but a formal check counts the full peak hour and our method can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x due to broken tracks, scaled from 24.7 minutes of video.
84.9% of the observed time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 8 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 35.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce approach speeds and give priority to those crossing.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

On the basis of a 9.7 minute video (582.0 s) at Lantern Road crossing we recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 28 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 53.0 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.3 s the vehicle was going at 53.6 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 2.2 s it was going at 44.1 km/h. In that recording 6 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 7 (1 in 7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 42.1-99.6% and 0.4-57.9% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson). By the study definition, 1 was serious (less than 1.5 s apart) and 5 were close passes (1.5-3.0 s). In 3 cases the person was first and in 3 cases the vehicle was first.

The worst cases measured by post-encroachment time were:
A serious near-miss with PET of 0.3 s involving a car at 44.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 5.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), and at 20.0 km/h impact it would be 0.6%.
A close pass with PET of 2.2 s involving a bus at 53.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 1.7%.
A close pass with PET of 1.6 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 33.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 1.5%.
A close pass with PET of 2.1 s involving a car at 22.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.0%.
A close pass with PET of 2.4 s involving a bus at 31.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.0%.
At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact and death risk for the last 4 cases would each be 0.0 km/h and 0.0%.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 9.7 minutes, with 7 pedestrian crossings and 28 moving vehicles counted. With that caveat, 93.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 9 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 51.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that the UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds and other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and establish pedestrian priority.

We are willing to share the video and the SAM tracking measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a raised table to slow vehicles and give priority to pupils crossing.

We can share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

A close pass with a gap of 2.7 s involved a van at 39.8 km/h.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this site to reduce speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the full measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The review found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 3 close passes (1.5-3.0 s), with person first in 2 cases and vehicle first in 4 cases.

The worst events were:

A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.1 s involving a car at 44.2 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 5.1%.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this crossing to lower speeds and provide a protected crossing point.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request to make the crossing outside the school safer

We are writing about the crossing on Orchard Lane outside our school. A 4.0 minute (240.0 s) video recording made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time measured 10 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles.

The headline result was that 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.7-65.2% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th-percentile speed of moving vehicles was 50.5 km/h. The recording these figures come from lasted 4.0 minutes. Using the standard definitions where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart, there was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car travelling at 32.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates a death risk of 1.8%. 
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s with a car travelling at 44.3 km/h. 
Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 37.3 km/h.

For engineering context we note only that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 4.0 minutes, so that calculation cannot be used here. Also 81.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 11 of them 12 s or more, longest 22.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for school children and other pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write as the school adjoining the Canal Road crossing about pedestrian safety.

In 36.8 minutes of video (2208.0 s) Crossing Watch recorded 8 crossings and 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 60.6 km/h. Near-misses like these occur every morning when school opens.

The analysis found 2 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart, with 3 cases where the person was first.

The most severe serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s involving a car travelling at 52.3 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would have been 10.0% according to Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+.

At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed in that case would have been 20.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.6%.

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s involving a car travelling at 42.8 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit would have been 4.5% and would have been 0.3% at 13.6 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s involving a car travelling at 55.2 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit would have been 5.0% and would have been 0.0% at 0.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 13 pedestrians and 16 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 36.8 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

Also 55.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 12 such gaps, 10 of them 12 s or more and longest 52.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with an approach speed table at this location.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write about pedestrian safety outside our school. A video review using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry measured the crossing for 37.5 minutes (2250.0 s). In that time 22 crossings and 20 vehicles were counted.

Of the 22 crossings, 3 of 22 (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 
Of the 22 crossings, 2 of 22 (1 in 11) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s of the person. 
Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile vehicle speed was 61.3 km/h. Children hit at these speeds face a far higher risk of death than adults.

The worst near-miss was a serious case with a car at 31.7 km/h passing 0.2 s from a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious case was a bus at 24.2 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s. For an adult hit at that speed the death risk is 0.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A close pass was a van at 57.7 km/h with a gap of 2.4 s.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 35 pedestrians and 32 moving vehicles an hour scaled from the 37.5 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour. 
In addition, 84.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 12 gaps with longest 9.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request to make the crossing outside the school safer

We are writing about the crossing on Orchard Lane outside our school. A 4.0 minute (240.0 s) video recording made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time measured 10 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles.

The headline result was that 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.7-65.2% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Using the standard definitions where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart, there was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car travelling at 32.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates a death risk of 1.8%. 
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s with a car travelling at 44.3 km/h. 
Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 37.3 km/h.

For engineering context we note only that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 4.0 minutes, so that calculation cannot be used here. Also 81.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 11 of them 12 s or more, longest 22.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for school children and other pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a raised zebra crossing at the crossing studied on Park Avenue crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write as the school using the crossing outside our premises. A Crossing Watch analysis of 38.6 minutes of video recorded 32 crossings and 30 vehicles.
The 85th percentile speed was 63.7 km/h. At its tightest, a vehicle and a person were on the same spot 0.5 s apart.
In that period 5 of 32 crossings (1 in 6.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.
Of those, 3 of 32 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s.
The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 5.3-32.8% and 2.0-25.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst near-misses recorded were as follows. A bus at 58.9 km/h was 1.0 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 16.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A motorcycle at 44.4 km/h was 0.5 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 5.2%.
A car at 42.8 km/h was 1.2 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%.
A car at 43.2 km/h was 2.3 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.3%.
A car at 34.8 km/h was 2.6 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.0%.
Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, calculated as 50 pedestrians and 47 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.6 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and our method can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests.
Also 72.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 8 gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 60.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for people crossing.
We are willing to share the underlying measurements and discuss the site in detail, and we can provide the video file on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Hill View Road

We measured traffic at the crossing on Hill View Road for 39.3 minutes. In that time we observed 34 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 60.0 km/h. A parent was injured here by a passing motorcycle earlier this year.

We recorded 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5 s to 3.0 s. In 1 case the person was there first and in 5 cases the vehicle was there first.

The most severe near-miss involved a car at 56.6 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 14.1% based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and above.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 28.6 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.3%.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.0 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 25.1 km/h with a gap of 0.6 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

Engineering indicators were calculated as follows. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 52 pedestrians and 32 vehicles per hour scaled from the video, noting that a formal check requires the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests. 45.3% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurement file for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 13.9% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+ car fronts, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 42.7 km/h with 0.5 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 4.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 14.3 km/h with 1.2 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, compared with 0.4% at 14.3 km/h.
A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 59.4 km/h with 2.3 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 2.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, compared with 0.0% at 0.0 km/h.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location.

We have the video and Crossing Watch SAM tracking measurements and are willing to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Re: Safety at School Lane crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table with 20 km/h zone markings at School Lane crossing.

A 5.6 minute video (336.0 s) at this crossing recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 41.1 km/h.
6 of 10 crossings (1 in 1.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.
4 of 10 crossings (1 in 2.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s. Most people crossing were unaccompanied schoolchildren rushing to class.
We note PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 5.6 minutes.

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing outside our school on Ring Road, where Crossing Watch analysis using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 8 moving vehicles in 6.1 minutes (366.0 s).

The 85th percentile speed was 47.9 km/h. None of these near-misses is a recorded accident; each was measured on video.

Overall, 3 of 8 crossings (1 in 2.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 8 (1 in 8) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 8.5-75.5% and 0.3-52.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most serious near-miss was an auto-rickshaw at 19.5 km/h with a gap of 1.3 s, with an adult death risk of 0.6% if hit by a car front at that speed (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), which would remain 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit with an impact speed of 19.5 km/h.

A second near-miss was a motorcycle at 48.1 km/h with a gap of 1.7 s, with an adult death risk of 4.5% if hit by a car front at that speed, which would be 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with an impact speed of 0.0 km/h.

A third near-miss was a van at 35.6 km/h with a gap of 2.8 s, with an adult death risk of 0.0% if hit by a car front at that speed, which would be 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with an impact speed of 0.0 km/h.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 6.1 minutes, so they were not calculated. 64.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 such gaps and a longest gap of 10.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the underlying video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Station Road crossing

We write as the school using the crossing outside our gate. Crossing Watch video covering 25.6 minutes (1536.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.9 km/h. 62.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more.

The analysis found 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Of the 8 potential conflicts, 4 had the person first, 2 had the vehicle first, and 0 had both at once.

The worst near-misses were:
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 59.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 18.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context, the video gives PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 from 19 pedestrians and 82 vehicles per hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 25.6 minutes not a full peak hour and our test shows broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. Also, 62.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 11 such gaps including 3 of 12 s or more and longest 74.2 s, with the caveat that first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We have the video and Crossing Watch data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Bridge Street crossing

Our school arranged Crossing Watch measurements at the Bridge Street crossing made by SAM tracking with road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In 29.3 minutes (1758.0 s) of video, 12 crossings and 29 vehicles were recorded, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h. Over 29.3 minutes 12 crossings occurred alongside 29 vehicles and the longest period without a moving vehicle at the crossing point was 77.5 s.

4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 12 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 9.9-65.1% and 2.1-48.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 2 serious near-misses included one with a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 52.8 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 10.5% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.1 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 2.8%.
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s with a car at 25.8 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 0.4%.
A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s with a motorcycle at 21.5 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 0.2%.

For context, PV2 was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 25 pedestrians and 59 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 29.3 minutes of video, but a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test.
63.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 7 such gaps, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h approach signs at this crossing.
We have retained the video files from the 29.3 minute recording and can share them on request for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Quarry Road crossing

We measured safety at the Quarry Road crossing using a video of 18.9 minutes covering 6 crossings and 21 vehicles. During this recording, 3 of 6 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 6 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 11.8-88.2% and 0.4-64.1% of crossings and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long. The 85th percentile speed was 49.6 km/h. The recording showed 1 serious near-miss in all.

The most serious near-miss was a bus that passed the same spot 0.9 s after a person. In that encounter the bus was travelling at 17.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second near-miss was a close pass with a gap of 1.6 s involving an auto-rickshaw. The auto-rickshaw in that pass was travelling at 47.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 47.5 km/h the estimated death risk is 5.4%.

A third near-miss was a close pass with a gap of 2.3 s involving a car. The car in that pass was travelling at 34.1 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 19 pedestrians and 67 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 18.9 minutes of video, though a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also, 67.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, based on 4 gaps, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to slow vehicles and give priority to people crossing.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

A car at 25.1 km/h was 0.0 s apart from a pedestrian. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the published death risk is 1.0%.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write as the school adjoining the Canal Road crossing about pedestrian safety.

In 36.8 minutes of video (2208.0 s) Crossing Watch recorded 8 crossings and 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 60.6 km/h. The van that came closest is driven by Mr. Ashok Varghese of the corner shop.

The analysis found 2 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart, with 3 cases where the person was first.

The most severe serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s involving a car travelling at 52.3 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would have been 10.0% according to Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+.

At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed in that case would have been 20.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.6%.

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s involving a car travelling at 42.8 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit would have been 4.5% and would have been 0.3% at 13.6 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s involving a car travelling at 55.2 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit would have been 5.0% and would have been 0.0% at 0.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 13 pedestrians and 16 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 36.8 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

Also 55.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 12 such gaps, 10 of them 12 s or more and longest 52.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Market Street crossing

I write as head of the school by Market Street crossing. A 6.0 minute video (360.0 s) of the crossing was analysed by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time). In that period we counted 12 pedestrian crossings and 26 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 56.0 km/h. The second serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 39.5 km/h with 1.2 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 3.4 %.
The third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 19.3 km/h with 0.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 0.6 %.
A close pass involved a car at 45.4 km/h with 2.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 0.4 %.
Another close pass involved a van at 18.4 km/h with 1.9 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 0.0 %.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.0. 81.1 % of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more, 1 of them 12 s or more, and longest 35.6 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and provide protected priority for pedestrians.

We have the video and measurements and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school on Lantern Road.

Crossing Watch measured 21.9 minutes of video showing 30 crossings and 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 52.6 mph.

There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass between 1.5 s and 3.0 s, all with the person first in 3 cases. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s with a car travelling at 47.1 km/h, which carries an adult death risk of 6.5% if hit by a car front, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. Another serious near-miss had a gap of 0.7 s with a bus travelling at 26.5 km/h, which carries an adult death risk of 1.1% if hit by a car front. A close pass had a gap of 2.5 s with a van travelling at 12.8 km/h.

Engineering review notes PV² = 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 21.9 minutes to 82 pedestrians and 27 moving vehicles an hour, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice. It also notes 51.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 11 such gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more and longest 15.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We ask you to install a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce speeds and protect pedestrians. We can share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Hill View Road

We measured traffic at the crossing on Hill View Road for 39.3 minutes. In that time we observed 34 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 60.0 km/h. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision.

We recorded 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5 s to 3.0 s. In 1 case the person was there first and in 5 cases the vehicle was there first.

The most severe near-miss involved a car at 56.6 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 14.1% based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and above.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 28.6 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.3%.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.0 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 25.1 km/h with a gap of 0.6 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

Engineering indicators were calculated as follows. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 52 pedestrians and 32 vehicles per hour scaled from the video, noting that a formal check requires the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests. 45.3% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurement file for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety at North Avenue crossing

We are writing to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school.

Measurements from a Crossing Watch survey over 6.9 minutes (414.0 s) recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.5 km/h. These results satisfy the official criteria for a pedestrian signal at this spot.

In that short period there was 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

The most serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s and involved a car at 16.9 km/h.

A separate close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s and involved a motorcycle at 44.4 km/h.

A separate close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s and involved a bus at 17.6 km/h.

For the car event, published figures for adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+) give an adult death risk if hit of 0.5% at 16.9 km/h.

Engineering context carries caveats: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 6.9 minutes, and 81.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more (4 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 41.7 s) with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request that the road authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect children crossing.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing on Park Avenue outside the school

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school arranged a Crossing Watch on the crossing on Park Avenue. In 6.9 minutes (414.0 s) we counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 47.9 km/h. The video showed 7 gaps of 12 s or more with no moving vehicle.

We record a serious near-miss as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass as 1.5-3.0 s apart. We observed 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, with 1 case where the person was first and 2 cases where the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a van at 45.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 44.2 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1% (same source).

A close pass involved a car at 22.1 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s.

We note that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 6.9 minutes. In this short sample 50.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 gaps of 6 s or more and 6 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 79.0 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We can share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Lantern Road

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lantern Road. We had 41.9 minutes of video reviewed by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time). In that time 22 people crossed and 29 vehicles passed, with an 85th percentile speed of 51.8 km/h. Mrs. Leela Fernandes, who drives the morning bus, caused the worst of these events.

The review found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 3 close passes (1.5-3.0 s), with person first in 2 cases and vehicle first in 4 cases.

The worst events were:

A second serious near-miss had a gap of 0.7 s and a car at 36.2 km/h.
A third serious near-miss had a gap of 0.4 s and a car at 35.4 km/h.
A fourth serious near-miss had a gap of 0.0 s and a car at 27.7 km/h.
A close pass had a gap of 1.9 s and a car at 36.4 km/h.
Person first was 3, vehicle first was 2 and both at once was 1.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 43 pedestrians and 26 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.6 minutes of video and a formal check counts the full peak hour. 41.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 5 gaps and longest 9.1 s and the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location. We are willing to share the measurement data and video excerpts for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school – Cedar Lane

We write concerning the crossing outside our school on Cedar Lane. An independent video review (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) observed 24.8 minutes (1488.0 s) at the site and counted 14 crossings and 19 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.9 km/h. The recording these figures come from lasted 24.8 minutes.

The review classified 3 events as serious, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 events as close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s. In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 52.2 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 10.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, which would fall to 0.2% at an impact of 8.4 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 50.2 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 8.5% if hit at that speed.

A third serious near-miss involved a van at 31.2 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 1.6% if hit at that speed.

A close pass involved a car at 55.2 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 33.1 km/h with a gap of 2.1 s.

The engineering note estimates PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 24.8 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice. 95.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, in 4 gaps with the longest 83.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. We can share the video and measurement details for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

We write as the school using Garden Road crossing. We measured the crossing by video for 11.5 minutes (690.0 s).

In that time we counted 12 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 49.6 km/h. 5 of 12 crossings (1 in 2.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 4 of 12 (1 in 3) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 15.2-72.3% and 9.9-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 11.5 minutes with 12 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles, so it is too short for a formal PV² assessment.

66.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 4 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 40.6 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) were:
A serious near-miss with pet of 0.8 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 50.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A serious near-miss with pet of 1.4 s involving a car at 32.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.9%.
A serious near-miss with pet of 1.1 s involving a motorcycle at 15.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%.
A serious near-miss with pet of 0.9 s involving a car at 12.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.
There was also 5 close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart: pet of 2.6 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 20.1 km/h.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Garden Road crossing to reduce vehicle speeds at the crossing point.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We write concerning the crossing on River Lane outside our school. We monitored the crossing by video for 24.7 minutes (1482.0 s) and counted 14 pedestrian crossings and 16 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 46.9 km/h. Parents see the same danger here at each school dismissal.

We recorded 1 serious near-miss defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart, with 2 cases where the vehicle arrived first, 0 where the person arrived first and 0 where both arrived at once.

The serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s and involved a car travelling at 41.4 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 4.0%, compared with 0.2% if impact were at 5.8 km/h under a 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

The close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s and involved a bus travelling at 30.5 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.1%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

For context, engineering estimates scale to 34 pedestrians and 39 vehicles an hour to give PV² = 0.0 x 10^8, but a formal check counts the full peak hour and our method can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x due to broken tracks, scaled from 24.7 minutes of video.
84.9% of the observed time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 8 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 35.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce approach speeds and give priority to those crossing.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Lantern Road

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lantern Road. We had 41.9 minutes of video reviewed by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time). In that time 22 people crossed and 29 vehicles passed, with an 85th percentile speed of 51.8 km/h. Every person in these near-misses was a pupil of our school.

The review found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 3 close passes (1.5-3.0 s), with person first in 2 cases and vehicle first in 4 cases.

The worst events were:
A serious near-miss with a gap of 0.2 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 51.0 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 9.1% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact).
A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.4 s involving a car at 44.5 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 5.2%.
A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.1 s involving a car at 44.2 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 5.1%.
A close pass with a gap of 1.9 s involving a van at 22.6 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 0.2%.
A close pass with a gap of 2.2 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 28.1 km/h.

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Mill Street crossing

We write on behalf of the school about the crossing at Mill Street crossing.

Crossing Watch video analysis covering 6.6 minutes (396.0 s) recorded 5 pedestrian crossings and 37 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 60.6 km/h. These figures come from a single recording and may differ on other days. There were 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. In this method serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s. Of the 5 crossings, 1 was person first, 4 were vehicle first and 0 were both at once.

One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s with a car at 53.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 11.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car at 22.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Engineering context is limited because PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.6 minutes. With that caveat, 44.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. That was 10 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, longest 9.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing on a speed table with 20 km/h zone signs at this location.

We can share the video and measurement log on request and welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir / Madam,

Re: Safety at Lake View Road crossing

In a Crossing Watch video of 33.6 minutes (2016.0 s) we measured 6 pedestrian crossings and 33 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 43.6 km/h. Most of the people seen crossing were schoolchildren on their way to class.

5 of 6 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 3 of 6 (1 in 2) were within 1.5 s.
Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 35.9-99.6% and 11.8-88.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 3 serious near-misses and 2 close passes were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s and involved a car at 35.2 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 2.3% for a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s and involved a car at 33.4 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 2.0% for a car front, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved a car at 17.8 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.5% for a car front, remaining 0.5% at an impact of 17.8 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s and involved a car at 22.2 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.4% for a car front, falling to 0.1% at an impact of 3.3 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.3 s and involved a bus at 44.8 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.4% for a car front, falling to 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h.

On engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, but this is scaled from only 33.6 minutes of video and a formal check counts the full peak hour with caveats about broken tracks.
73.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 8 of 12 s or more and longest gap 76.8 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority.

We can share the full video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

We are writing about the pedestrian crossing outside our school at Lantern Road crossing.

A video recording of 3.9 minutes (234.0 s) was made and analysed with SAM tracking. In that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 58.5 km/h. The closest near-miss measured had a time gap of 0.9 s.

Of the 4 crossings, 2 of 4 (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 4 (1 in 2) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 6.8-93.2% and 6.8-93.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 2 serious near-misses with less than 1.5 s between pedestrian and vehicle and 0 close passes with 1.5-3.0 s.

The 2 serious near-misses were:
One involved a car at 55.0 km/h with 1.4 s between pedestrian and moving vehicle at the same spot. If hit by a car front at that speed, the adult death risk is 12.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another involved an auto-rickshaw at 19.6 km/h with 0.9 s between pedestrian and moving vehicle at the same spot. If hit, the adult death risk given for that speed is 0.6% (same source, for adults hit by a car front).

For context, 62.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap and 1 gap of 12 s or more, longest 66.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² and hourly rates cannot be assessed from this video because at least 15 minutes of video is needed and this one is 3.9 minutes.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect children crossing.

We can share the video and measurement data on request and welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.
