LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school on Mill Street.

Measurements from 44.3 minutes of video recorded 35 crossings and 22 vehicles. 4 of 35 crossings (1 in 8.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 35 (1 in 18) were within 1.5 s. The 85th percentile speed was 55.2 km/h. Several children have been hurt at this crossing since the term began.

There were 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. One serious near-miss involved a van at 52.0 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s. Another serious near-miss involved a car at 18.4 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s. One close pass involved a motorcycle at 33.5 km/h with a gap of 1.7 s. Another close pass involved a van at 25.0 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 52.0 km/h the death-risk figure is 9.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 44.3 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour. 45.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 2 such gaps and a longest gap of 47.5 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect people crossing.

We would be happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. The video covered 21.4 minutes and showed 11 crossings and 22 vehicles.

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing on Park Avenue outside the school

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school arranged a Crossing Watch on the crossing on Park Avenue. In 6.9 minutes (414.0 s) we counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 47.9 km/h. 7 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video.

We record a serious near-miss as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass as 1.5-3.0 s apart. We observed 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, with 1 case where the person was first and 2 cases where the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a van at 45.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 44.2 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1% (same source).

A close pass involved a car at 22.1 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s.

We note that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 6.9 minutes. In this short sample 50.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 gaps of 6 s or more and 6 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 79.0 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We can share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write to request a safety improvement at the crossing outside our school. We commissioned a Crossing Watch measurement using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry to assess post-encroachment time.

Over 11.1 minutes (666.0 s) the video counted 12 pedestrian crossings and 11 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.4 km/h. Children hit at these speeds face a far higher risk of death than adults. In that period 4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 3 of 12 crossings (1 in 4) were within 1.5 s.
Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 9.9-65.1% and 5.5-57.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The video found 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. The worst serious near-miss was 1.2 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 47.4 km/h. A second serious near-miss was 0.2 s apart involving a van at 44.0 km/h. A third serious near-miss was 0.4 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 13.1 km/h. The close pass was 1.9 s apart involving a car at 50.1 km/h.
For adults hit by a car front, Rosén and Sander 2009 gives an adult death risk if hit of 6.7% for the 47.4 km/h case, 5.0% for the 44.0 km/h case, 0.3% for the 13.1 km/h case, and 3.2% for the 50.1 km/h case. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk for the 47.4 km/h case, 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk for the 44.0 km/h case, 13.1 km/h with 0.3% adult death risk for the 13.1 km/h case, and 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk for the 50.1 km/h case.

For context, PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 11.1 minutes. The recording also shows 66.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 3 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 33.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h markings at this location.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Bridge Street crossing

Our school arranged Crossing Watch measurements at the Bridge Street crossing made by SAM tracking with road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In 29.3 minutes (1758.0 s) of video, 12 crossings and 29 vehicles were recorded, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h. Children hit at these speeds face a far higher risk of death than adults.

4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 12 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 9.9-65.1% and 2.1-48.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 2 serious near-misses included one with a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 52.8 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 10.5% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.1 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 2.8%.
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s with a car at 25.8 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 0.4%.
A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s with a motorcycle at 21.5 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 0.2%.

For context, PV2 was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 25 pedestrians and 59 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 29.3 minutes of video, but a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test.
63.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 7 such gaps, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h approach signs at this crossing.
We have retained the video files from the 29.3 minute recording and can share them on request for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the River Lane crossing outside our school. A video recording of 4.7 minutes (282.0 s) captured 4 pedestrian crossings and 25 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 47.1 km/h. The recording showed 1 serious near-miss in all.

In that recording, 4 of 4 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 3 of 4 (1 in 1.3) within 1.5 s. Serious is defined as less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s. In total there were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. In 1 case the person was first, in 3 cases the vehicle was first, and in 0 cases both were at once.

The worst events were as follows. 1 serious near-miss involved a car at 39.7 km/h with a gap of 1.3 s. 1 serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h with a gap of 0.6 s. 1 serious near-miss involved a car at 14.3 km/h with a gap of 1.3 s. 1 close pass involved a van at 31.8 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, gives an adult death risk if hit of 3.5% for the 39.7 km/h car, 2.9% for the 37.7 km/h auto-rickshaw, 0.4% for the 14.3 km/h car, and 0.0% for the 31.8 km/h van. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% risk for the 39.7 km/h car, 20.0 km/h with 0.6% risk for the 37.7 km/h auto-rickshaw, 14.3 km/h with 0.4% risk for the 14.3 km/h car, and 0.0 km/h with 0.0% risk for the 31.8 km/h van.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 4.7 minutes with 4 pedestrian crossings and 25 moving vehicles. Also, 97.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 1 gap, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 65.8 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds; other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h signs and markings at this location.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning safety at the Canal Road crossing outside our school. We commissioned a Crossing Watch video assessment using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time.

In that recording, 4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 12 (1 in 4) were within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 9.9-65.1% and 5.5-57.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the timed encounters, 2 had the person first and 2 had the vehicle first.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). The most severe serious near-miss involved a car at 54.1 km/h with a time gap of 0.8 s. At that speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 11.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), which would be 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h. A second serious near-miss involved a car at 48.4 km/h with a time gap of 1.4 s. At that speed the adult death risk if hit is 7.3%, which would be 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h. A third serious near-miss involved a van at 18.0 km/h with a time gap of 1.3 s. At that speed the adult death risk if hit is 0.5%, which would remain 0.5% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 18.0 km/h. The close pass involved a car at 28.3 km/h with a time gap of 1.8 s. At that speed the adult death risk if hit is 0.6%, which would be 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h.

For context, engineering guidance notes that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video, while this recording is only 6.6 minutes, and that 97.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more, 3 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 25.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at the Canal Road crossing to slow approaching traffic and give clear priority to people crossing.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at this location.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing on Park Avenue outside the school

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school arranged a Crossing Watch on the crossing on Park Avenue. In 6.9 minutes (414.0 s) we counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 47.9 km/h.

We record a serious near-miss as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass as 1.5-3.0 s apart. We observed 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, with 1 case where the person was first and 2 cases where the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a van at 45.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 44.2 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1% (same source).

A close pass involved a car at 22.1 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s.

We note that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 6.9 minutes. In this short sample 50.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 gaps of 6 s or more and 6 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 79.0 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location. Without intervention, a child is likely to be killed at this crossing within the next 12 months.

We can share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school

Dear Sir/Madam,

We asked for measurements at the Ring Road crossing. In 28.9 minutes 8 people were seen crossing and 12 vehicles were counted.

The headline finding is that 6 of 8 crossings (1 in 1.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 8 (1 in 2) within 1.5 s.

A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s with a van at 31.3 km/h; the adult death risk if hit is 1.7%.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location.

We are happy to share the underlying video and measurements for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request to make the crossing outside the school safer

We are writing about the crossing on Orchard Lane outside our school. A 4.0 minute (240.0 s) video recording made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time measured 10 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles.

The headline result was that 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.7-65.2% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th-percentile speed of moving vehicles was 50.5 km/h. We would be glad to walk the crossing with your engineers whenever it suits them. Using the standard definitions where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart, there was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car travelling at 32.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates a death risk of 1.8%. 
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s with a car travelling at 44.3 km/h. 
Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 37.3 km/h.

For engineering context we note only that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 4.0 minutes, so that calculation cannot be used here. Also 81.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 11 of them 12 s or more, longest 22.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for school children and other pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning safety at the Canal Road crossing outside our school. We commissioned a Crossing Watch video assessment using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time.

In 6.6 minutes (396.0 s) of video, 12 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles were counted, with an 85th percentile speed of 53.7 km/h. In total, 3 close passes were measured. In that recording, 4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 12 (1 in 4) were within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 9.9-65.1% and 5.5-57.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the timed encounters, 2 had the person first and 2 had the vehicle first.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). The most severe serious near-miss involved a car at 54.1 km/h with a time gap of 0.8 s. At that speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 11.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), which would be 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h. A second serious near-miss involved a car at 48.4 km/h with a time gap of 1.4 s. At that speed the adult death risk if hit is 7.3%, which would be 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h. A third serious near-miss involved a van at 18.0 km/h with a time gap of 1.3 s. At that speed the adult death risk if hit is 0.5%, which would remain 0.5% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 18.0 km/h. The close pass involved a car at 28.3 km/h with a time gap of 1.8 s. At that speed the adult death risk if hit is 0.6%, which would be 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h.

For context, engineering guidance notes that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video, while this recording is only 6.6 minutes, and that 97.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more, 3 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 25.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at the Canal Road crossing to slow approaching traffic and give clear priority to people crossing.

We would be pleased to share the video and SAM tracking data for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety work at Park Avenue crossing

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at Park Avenue crossing.

In a video of 16.8 minutes (1008.0 s) there were 35 crossings and 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.3 km/h. At its tightest, a vehicle and a person were on the same spot 0.2 s apart. Using SAM tracking, 2 events were classified as serious where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 0 were close passes (1.5-3.0 s). In 1 case the vehicle was first and in 1 case both were at once, with 0 cases where the person was first.

The worst near misses were:
One serious near miss involved a bus at 51.4 km/h with 0.2 s between road users. If an adult had been hit by the front of a car at that speed, the published adult death risk is 9.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
A second serious near miss involved a motorcycle at 20.7 km/h with 0.0 s between road users. At that speed the published adult death risk if hit by a car front is 0.6%, also 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

Preliminary engineering notes, with caveats, are that PV² was scaled to 0.0 x 10^8 from 125 pedestrians and 36 moving vehicles an hour based on 16.8 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour and our test showed tracking can count 1.3x the true pedestrian count, and that 94.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more (3 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, longest 7.7 s), but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We can share the video and measurements on request and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing outside our school on Mill Street. Crossing Watch measured 11 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles in 6.7 minutes (402.0 s) of video using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time.

In that recording 3 of 11 crossings (1 in 3.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 11 (1 in 11) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.0-61.0% and 0.2-41.3% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s with a car travelling at 49.5 km/h. The video showed 11 gaps of 12 s or more with no moving vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front that speed carries an 8.0% death risk, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h with an impact at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second near-miss was a close pass with a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s with a van travelling at 40.9 km/h.

A third near-miss was a close pass with a post-encroachment time of 2.8 s with a van travelling at 57.6 km/h.

The 85th percentile speed was 56.1 km/h. Engineering context is limited because PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.7 minutes. In this short recording 82.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps of 6 s or more and 2 of them 12 s or more and the longest gap 35.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We can share the video and measurement file for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Bridge Street crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

We are writing as the school adjoining Bridge Street crossing to request a safety improvement based on video measurements made by Crossing Watch.

What was measured: In 3.0 minutes, 180.0 s, we counted 4 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 49.2 km/h. 43.8% of the time was inside gaps of 12 s or more. 4 of 4 crossings, 1 in 1, had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 4 crossings, 1 in 1, were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 39.8-100.0% and 39.8-100.0% of crossings and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long. There were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 0 close passes, defined as 1.5-3.0 s. Of the 4 serious events, 3 had the person first, 1 had the vehicle first and 0 had both at once.

Worst near-misses: One serious event had a car at 51.7 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 9.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h. One serious event had a car at 50.3 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h. One serious event had a car at 46.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 6.2%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 6.4 km/h. One serious event had a van at 23.1 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h. Risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén and Sander 2009.

Engineering context: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 3.0. 43.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 gaps of 6 s or more, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 52.2 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect children and other pedestrians crossing where they need to.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and to meet on site.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school – Cedar Lane

We write concerning the crossing outside our school on Cedar Lane. An independent video review (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) observed 24.8 minutes (1488.0 s) at the site and counted 14 crossings and 19 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.9 km/h.

The review classified 3 events as serious, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 events as close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s. In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 52.2 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 10.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, which would fall to 0.2% at an impact of 8.4 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 50.2 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 8.5% if hit at that speed.

A third serious near-miss involved a van at 31.2 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 1.6% if hit at that speed.

A close pass involved a car at 55.2 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 33.1 km/h with a gap of 2.1 s.

The engineering note estimates PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 24.8 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice. 95.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, in 4 gaps with the longest 83.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. More than 100 children cross here every morning, making intervention urgent. We can share the video and measurement details for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety at North Avenue crossing

We are writing to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school.

Measurements from a Crossing Watch survey over 6.9 minutes (414.0 s) recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.5 km/h. The video showed 4 gaps of 12 s or more with no moving vehicle.

In that short period there was 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

The most serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s and involved a car at 16.9 km/h.

A separate close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s and involved a motorcycle at 44.4 km/h.

A separate close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s and involved a bus at 17.6 km/h.

For the car event, published figures for adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+) give an adult death risk if hit of 0.5% at 16.9 km/h.

Engineering context carries caveats: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 6.9 minutes, and 81.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more (4 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 41.7 s) with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request that the road authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect children crossing.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write on behalf of the school about the crossing on North Avenue (North Avenue crossing).

Over 7.1 minutes (426.0 s) of video we recorded 4 pedestrian crossings and 18 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 47.7 km/h. Near-misses like these occur every morning when school opens.

In that time there were 4 serious near-misses and 0 close passes. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s. In 2 cases the pedestrian was first, in 1 case the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both arrived at once.

The 4 serious near-misses were:
A motorcycle at 39.7 km/h was 0.4 s from a pedestrian. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 3.5% compared with 0.6% at a 20.0 km/h impact.
A motorcycle at 31.4 km/h was 0.5 s from a pedestrian. Adult death risk 1.7% compared with 0.6% at a 20.0 km/h impact.
An auto-rickshaw at 27.7 km/h was 0.0 s from a pedestrian. Adult death risk 1.2% compared with 0.6% at a 20.0 km/h impact.
A bus at 19.0 km/h was 1.4 s from a pedestrian. Adult death risk 0.6% compared with 0.6% at a 19.0 km/h impact.
All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosen and Sander 2009, adults 15 plus.

Engineering note: PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 7.1 minutes. Counted: 4 pedestrian crossings, 18 moving vehicles. 87.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 1 gap, 0 of them 12 s or more, longest 8.7 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. Guidance notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location to lower speeds and provide protected crossing gaps.

We are happy to share the tracking data and video file on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

We write regarding the safety of the crossing outside our school on Market Street.

A further close pass had a PET of 2.7 s with a van at 59.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the recorded death risk is 0.0%.
At a 20 km/h limit the modelled adult death risks for these events would fall to 0.0%, 0.0%, 0.6%, 0.0% and 0.0% respectively.

Given these measurements we request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We are willing to share the video and tracking data for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Hill View Road

We measured traffic at the crossing on Hill View Road for 39.3 minutes. In that time we observed 34 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 60.0 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.7 s the vehicle was going at 28.6 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 0.3 s it was going at 56.6 km/h.

We recorded 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5 s to 3.0 s. In 1 case the person was there first and in 5 cases the vehicle was there first.

The most severe near-miss involved a car at 56.6 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 14.1% based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and above.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 28.6 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.3%.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.0 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 25.1 km/h with a gap of 0.6 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

Engineering indicators were calculated as follows. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 52 pedestrians and 32 vehicles per hour scaled from the video, noting that a formal check requires the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests. 45.3% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurement file for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. Many of these drivers were not watching the road at all.

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write to request a safer crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch video under road-plane geometry and SAM tracking recorded 37.6 minutes (2256.0 s) at the Lantern Road crossing, observing 10 crossings and 6 vehicles.

In that short recording, 4 of 10 crossings (1 in 2.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 2 of 10 (1 in 5) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 12.2-73.8% and 2.5-55.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). By definition a serious near-miss is less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

The 85th percentile speed was 61.2 km/h. The video showed 0 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle.

The most severe near-miss involved a van at 58.7 km/h passing 1.0 s after the person had been on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 16.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss involved a car at 36.2 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.6%.

A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 24.0 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%.

A further close pass involved a bus at 16.8 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%.

Engineering context, with caveats: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 37.6 minutes to 16 pedestrians and 10 moving vehicles per hour, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 47.6% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 such gaps and a longest gap of 11.7 s, while the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing on a speed table at this location and consider a 20 km/h zone with signs.

We are willing to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We asked for measurements at the Ring Road crossing. In 28.9 minutes 8 people were seen crossing and 12 vehicles were counted.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location.

We are happy to share the underlying video and measurements for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén and Sander 2009 gives an adult death risk if hit of 6.7% for the 50.1 km/h case, 5.0% for the 44.0 km/h case, 0.3% for the 13.1 km/h case, and 3.2% for the 47.4 km/h case. For context, PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 11.1 minutes. The recording also shows 66.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 3 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 33.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

On the basis of a 9.7 minute video (582.0 s) at Lantern Road crossing we recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 28 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 53.0 km/h. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision. In that recording 6 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 7 (1 in 7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 42.1-99.6% and 0.4-57.9% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson). By the study definition, 1 was serious (less than 1.5 s apart) and 5 were close passes (1.5-3.0 s). In 3 cases the person was first and in 3 cases the vehicle was first.

The worst cases measured by post-encroachment time were:
A serious near-miss with PET of 0.3 s involving a car at 44.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 5.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), and at 20.0 km/h impact it would be 0.6%.
A close pass with PET of 2.2 s involving a bus at 53.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 1.7%.
A close pass with PET of 1.6 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 33.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 1.5%.
A close pass with PET of 2.1 s involving a car at 22.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.0%.
A close pass with PET of 2.4 s involving a bus at 31.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.0%.
At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact and death risk for the last 4 cases would each be 0.0 km/h and 0.0%.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 9.7 minutes, with 7 pedestrian crossings and 28 moving vehicles counted. With that caveat, 93.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 9 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 51.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that the UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds and other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and establish pedestrian priority.

We are willing to share the video and the SAM tracking measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

Our school arranged a video measurement at North Avenue crossing for 3.7 minutes (222.0 s).

In that recording 12 pedestrian crossings and 41 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 61.3 km/h. At its tightest, a vehicle and a person were on the same spot 0.3 s apart. 6 of 12 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 21.1-78.9% and 9.9-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Serious near-misses were defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s) were recorded.

The worst incidents were as follows. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car at 58.3 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 16.1%. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with a car at 23.2 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.8%. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s with an auto-rickshaw at 16.5 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.4%. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s with a car at 12.6 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.3%. One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a bus at 35.7 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 2.4%. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front per Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

For context, 83.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more, 0 of them 12 s or more and longest gap 10.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 3.7 minutes, so counts are limited to 12 pedestrian crossings and 41 moving vehicles.

We request a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h speed table and warning signs at this location to lower approach speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We can share the video and measurement data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write to request a safety improvement at the crossing outside our school. We commissioned a Crossing Watch measurement using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry to assess post-encroachment time.

Over 11.1 minutes (666.0 s) the video counted 12 pedestrian crossings and 11 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.4 mph. In that period 4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 3 of 12 crossings (1 in 4) were within 1.5 s.
Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 9.9-65.1% and 5.5-57.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The video found 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. The worst serious near-miss was 1.2 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 47.4 km/h. A second serious near-miss was 0.2 s apart involving a van at 44.0 km/h. A third serious near-miss was 0.4 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 13.1 km/h. The close pass was 1.9 s apart involving a car at 50.1 km/h.
For adults hit by a car front, Rosén and Sander 2009 gives an adult death risk if hit of 6.7% for the 47.4 km/h case, 5.0% for the 44.0 km/h case, 0.3% for the 13.1 km/h case, and 3.2% for the 50.1 km/h case. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk for the 47.4 km/h case, 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk for the 44.0 km/h case, 13.1 km/h with 0.3% adult death risk for the 13.1 km/h case, and 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk for the 50.1 km/h case.

For context, PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 11.1 minutes. The recording also shows 66.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 3 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 33.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h markings at this location.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and associated signs at this location.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

- One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with a car at 39.5 km/h. Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by a car front gives 3.4% adult death risk if hit, compared to 0.6% death risk if impact were at 20.0 km/h with a 20 km/h limit.
- One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 17.8 km/h.

For context on gaps, 68.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps of 6 s and 2 gaps of 12 s, longest 25.9 s. Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We write concerning the crossing on River Lane outside our school. We monitored the crossing by video for 24.7 minutes (1482.0 s) and counted 14 pedestrian crossings and 16 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 46.9 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.9 s the vehicle was going at 30.5 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 2.1 s it was going at 41.4 km/h.

We recorded 1 serious near-miss defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart, with 2 cases where the vehicle arrived first, 0 where the person arrived first and 0 where both arrived at once.

The serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s and involved a car travelling at 41.4 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 4.0%, compared with 0.2% if impact were at 5.8 km/h under a 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

The close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s and involved a bus travelling at 30.5 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.1%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

For context, engineering estimates scale to 34 pedestrians and 39 vehicles an hour to give PV² = 0.0 x 10^8, but a formal check counts the full peak hour and our method can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x due to broken tracks, scaled from 24.7 minutes of video.
84.9% of the observed time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 8 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 35.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce approach speeds and give priority to those crossing.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The 85th percentile speed was 57.4 km/h. By these figures the crossing already qualifies for a signal-controlled crossing.

By definition a serious near-miss is less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s apart.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with a car at 57.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 14.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.5 s with a car at 39.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.3%.
A close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a car at 21.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.
A further close pass had a PET of 2.7 s with a van at 59.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the recorded death risk is 0.0%.
At a 20 km/h limit the modelled adult death risks for these events would fall to 0.0%, 0.0%, 0.6%, 0.0% and 0.0% respectively.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside our school on Brook Street

We asked Crossing Watch to measure the crossing outside our school using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In 36.1 minutes (2166.0 s) of video they counted 13 crossings and 26 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 47.9 mph. There were 6 gaps of 6 s or more, 2 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 58.6 s.

By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s apart. We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. In 3 cases the person arrived first and in 2 cases the vehicle arrived first.

The most serious near-miss left 0.4 s between pedestrian and a car.
The car in that near-miss was at 48.1 km/h.
At that speed an adult hit by a car front has a 7.1% death risk, compared with 0.6% death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss left 1.0 s between pedestrian and an auto-rickshaw.
The auto-rickshaw in that near-miss was at 28.7 km/h.
At that speed an adult hit by a car front has a 1.3% death risk, compared with 0.6% death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

A close pass left 1.8 s between pedestrian and a car.
The car in that close pass was at 50.7 km/h.
A close pass left 2.1 s between pedestrian and a bus.
The bus in that close pass was at 33.4 km/h.
A close pass left 2.5 s between pedestrian and a van.
The van in that close pass was at 15.2 km/h.

For engineering context the scaled PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 22 pedestrians and 43 vehicles an hour, but this is scaled from 36.1 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice.
43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to reduce vehicle speeds.

We have retained the video measurements and can share the video files on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Mill Street crossing following a video recording of 4.0 minutes (240.0 s) at the site. In that time we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 11 moving vehicles.

4 of 8 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person; 3 of 8 (1 in 2.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 15.7-84.3% and 8.5-75.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 4 cases, 3 were serious (less than 1.5 s) and 1 was a close pass (1.5-3.0 s).

The worst near-misses were as follows. 1 serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s with a motorcycle travelling at 38.8 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 3.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). The recording these figures come from lasted 4.0 minutes.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s with a car travelling at 29.8 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 1.4%.
A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s with a bus travelling at 23.2 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 0.8%.
1 close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a van travelling at 31.3 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 1.7%.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 4.0. Counted: 8 pedestrian crossings, 11 moving vehicles. 76.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 5 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 37.1 s (the first and last are cut short by the video). UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2): 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds; other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on River Lane

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the River Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch recorded 25 crossings in 36.0 minutes with 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.9 km/h. At its tightest, a vehicle and a person were on the same spot 1.3 s apart.

In that period 2 of 25 crossings (1 in 12) were serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 of 25 (1 in 12) were within 3 s. Exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 1.0-26.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most severe was a bus at 52.9 km/h passing 0.1 s after a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.6% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

The second serious near-miss was a van at 22.9 km/h passing 1.3 s after a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 36.0 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice. Also, 62.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 3 such gaps and longest 81.8 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pupils crossing.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school commissioned a video survey of the Garden Road crossing. In 16.9 minutes (1014.0 s) of video, 5 crossings and 8 vehicles were observed. 3 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 3 of 5 (1 in 1.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 14.7-94.7% and 14.7-94.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.6-8.8 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 45.6 km/h. The closest of these near-misses was the fault of Mr. Tarun Mehra, who runs the tea stall.

There were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.4 s with a car at 46.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 6.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

Another serious near-miss had a gap of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 22.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

A third serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s with a car at 17.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%, compared with 0.5% at 17.5 km/h.

Engineering context from the survey, with caveats: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 18 pedestrians and 28 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 16.9 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 70.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 10 gaps, 9 of them 12 s or more, longest 23.5 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table to lower vehicle speeds and protect people crossing.

We are willing to share the full video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Lantern Road crossing

During 43.6 minutes of video we counted 31 crossings and 19 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.0 km/h. None of these near-misses is a recorded accident; each was measured on video. We request you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location. We are willing to share the measurement data and video excerpts for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I write about the crossing outside our school on Cedar Lane. A video-based count over 37.7 minutes recorded 36 crossings and 12 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.6 km/h. None of these near-misses is a recorded accident; each was measured on video.

The review found 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass of 1.5 to 3.0 s. In that period 3 crossings were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first.

One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 49.0 km/h with 1.2 s between pedestrian and vehicle.

For an adult hit by a car front at 49.0 km/h the death risk is 7.7% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 47.5 km/h with 0.5 s between pedestrian and vehicle.

For an adult hit by a car front at 47.5 km/h the death risk is 6.7%.

A further serious near-miss involved a van at 34.3 km/h with 1.0 s between pedestrian and vehicle.

For an adult hit by a car front at 34.3 km/h the death risk is 2.2%.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 21.8 km/h with 0.5 s between pedestrian and vehicle.

For an adult hit by a car front at 21.8 km/h the death risk is 0.7%.

One close pass involved a bus at 38.3 km/h with 1.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle.

For an adult hit by a car front at 38.3 km/h the death risk is 1.4%.

Engineering notes from the same video show PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 57 pedestrians and 19 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 37.7 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount by 1.3x the true count in a drone test. The video also showed 93.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 12 such gaps and 5 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 13.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We would be pleased to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school

We measured activity at the crossing outside the school for 40.6 minutes (2436.0 s). In that time we recorded 22 crossings and 29 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 41.9 km/h. The video showed 1 gap of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle.

The most serious was a car at 40.2 km/h passing 1.0 s after the person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second event was a motorcycle at 31.3 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A third event was a van at 42.5 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A fourth event was a car at 23.0 km/h with a gap of 2.9 s.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

At a 20 km/h limit the modelled adult death risks for these events would fall to 0.0%, 0.0%, 0.6%, 0.0% and 0.0% respectively.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, from 58 pedestrians and 64 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 36.4 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour. 69.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 such gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more and the longest 56.1 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

Given these measurements we request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We are willing to share the video and tracking data for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
Dear Sir / Madam,

At Cedar Lane crossing, video covering 30.7 minutes / 1842.0 s recorded 6 crossings and 34 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 56.4 km/h. 5 of 6 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 6 crossings (1 in 1.5) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 35.9-99.6% and 22.3-95.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson). Ranges for a recording this long: 1.6-11.7 and 1.1-10.2 people (Poisson). 4 were serious near-misses under 1.5 s and 1 was a close pass at 1.5-3.0 s.

The closest serious near-miss was 0.3 s apart involving a van at 50.8 km/h. Adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 8.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A serious near-miss was 1.4 s apart involving a motorcycle at 45.3 km/h. Adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 5.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A serious near-miss was 1.4 s apart involving a car at 17.4 km/h. Adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A serious near-miss was 0.7 s apart involving a car at 13.5 km/h. Adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A close pass was 2.3 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 32.0 km/h.

PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 12 pedestrians and 66 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 30.7 minutes of video. A formal check counts the full peak hour and counts can be 1.3x the true count in our drone test. 59.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 11 gaps of 6 s or more and 7 of 12 s or more, with longest 56.1 s. The gaps at start and end are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing at Cedar Lane crossing. We offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing on Station Road outside our school, where we made video measurements using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time.

During 6.1 minutes (366.0 s) we observed 12 pedestrian crossings and 20 vehicles.
The 85th percentile speed was 30.3 km/h. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week.
3 of 12 crossings (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 12 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s.
If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 5.5-57.2% and 2.1-48.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

For context on gaps, 50.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 12 gaps, 6 of them 12 s or more, longest 59.7 s, with the first and last cut short by the video.
PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 6.1, with 12 crossings and 20 vehicles counted.

By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.
We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s and involved a car at 29.3 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 1.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved a car at 17.3 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.5%, compared with 0.5% at 17.3 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s and involved a van at 32.1 km/h.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and provide protected gaps.

We have the video and measurements available and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority,

We are writing about safety at the River Lane crossing.

We arranged a Crossing Watch count lasting 7.6 minutes (456.0 s). In that time we counted 3 pedestrian crossings and 1 moving vehicles. Of the crossings, 1 of 3 (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 3 (1 in 3) within 1.5 s. The 85th percentile speed was 50.4 km/h. Near-misses like these occur every morning when school opens.

For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 7.6. Also 81.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 gaps of 6 s or more and 5 of 12 s or more, longest 54.5 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We recorded 1 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 0 close passes (1.5 to 3.0 s).

The worst case was a serious event involving a van travelling at 46.6 km/h. The time gap between road users at the conflict point was 0.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 6.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to reduce speeds and provide protected priority for people crossing.


Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Road Authority,

The school arranged Crossing Watch tracking at Garden Road crossing. In 8.8 minutes of video there were six pedestrian crossings and 12 moving vehicles with 85th percentile speed of 55.3 km/h.

The review found 4 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass means 1.5-3.0 s.

Counts were 2 with person first and 3 with vehicle first and 0 with both at once.

The bus serious encounter had a gap of 0.3 s. The bus speed was 55.3 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 12.8 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 20.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.6 %.

The car serious encounter had a gap of 0.3 s. The car speed was 48.0 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 7.0 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 20.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.6 %.

The car serious encounter had a gap of 1.1 s. The car speed was 39.1 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 3.3 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 0.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.0 %.

The van serious encounter had a gap of 0.9 s. The van speed was 36.1 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 2.5 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 16.5 km/h with adult death risk of 0.4 %.

The van close pass encounter had a gap of 1.6 s. The van speed was 25.2 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 0.8 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 0.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.0 %.

Risk figures are from Rosén and Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

On engineering, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this video is 8.8. In this video 62.3 % of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and give priority to crossing pupils.

We offer to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

During 32.2 minutes of video at River Lane crossing (1932.0 s) Crossing Watch recorded 12 crossings and 24 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.3 km/h. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision.

The analysis found 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5-3.0 s. In 4 cases the person was there first and in 1 case the vehicle was there first. One serious near-miss had a gap of 1.3 s between road users and the auto-rickshaw was travelling at 58.7 km/h, which carries an adult death risk of 16.5% if hit by a car front, based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. A second serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s and the auto-rickshaw was travelling at 36.4 km/h, with an adult death risk of 2.6% if hit. A third serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s and the car was travelling at 17.8 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.5% if hit. A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s and the auto-rickshaw was travelling at 45.1 km/h, with an adult death risk of 3.5% if hit. A further close pass had a gap of 2.9 s and the car was travelling at 12.9 km/h.

The engineering indicators were scaled from this short sample: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 22 pedestrians and 45 moving vehicles an hour, and a formal check counts the full peak hour. 67.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap and a longest gap of 80.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location and we offer to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully
The Principal

Dear Road Authority,

I write on behalf of the school regarding the Garden Road crossing.

We commissioned a 9.5 minute (570.0 s) video survey at the crossing. In that time 3 pedestrian crossings and 24 moving vehicles were recorded. The 85th percentile speed was 62.6 km/h. Once this fix is built, no one will die at this crossing. 3 of 3 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 3 (1 in 1.5) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.2-100.0% and 9.4-99.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 2 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s apart); the vehicle arrived first in 3 of 3 cases.

The worst serious near-miss involved a car at 56.4 km/h passing 0.8 s from the person, with an adult death risk of 13.9% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), falling to 0.0 km/h impact and 0.0% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

A second serious near-miss involved a car at 22.3 km/h passing 0.2 s from the person, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit, and 20.0 km/h impact with 0.6% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

A close pass involved a bus at 37.2 km/h passing 2.8 s from the person.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 9.5 minutes, so those rates cannot be reliably used. 93.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 6 gaps of 12 s or more, the longest 32.9 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at the Garden Road crossing to reduce speeds and provide priority where the 3 crossings were observed.

We can share the video and the full measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) on request and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

During 32.2 minutes of video at River Lane crossing (1932.0 s) Crossing Watch recorded 12 crossings and 24 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.3 km/h.

The analysis found 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5-3.0 s. In 4 cases the person was there first and in 1 case the vehicle was there first. One serious near-miss had a gap of 1.3 s between road users and the auto-rickshaw was travelling at 58.7 km/h, which carries an adult death risk of 16.5% if hit by a car front, based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. A second serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s and the auto-rickshaw was travelling at 36.4 km/h, with an adult death risk of 2.6% if hit. A third serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s and the car was travelling at 17.8 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.5% if hit. A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s and the auto-rickshaw was travelling at 45.1 km/h, with an adult death risk of 3.5% if hit. A further close pass had a gap of 2.9 s and the car was travelling at 12.9 km/h.

The engineering indicators were scaled from this short sample: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 22 pedestrians and 45 moving vehicles an hour, and a formal check counts the full peak hour. 67.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap and a longest gap of 80.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location and we offer to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully
The Principal

We write regarding the River Lane crossing. In 28.6 minutes of video we recorded 24 crossings and 48 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 58.5 km/h. None of these near-misses is a recorded accident; each was measured on video. A third serious near-miss involved a car at 42.1 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.3%.

A fourth serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 34.4 km/h with a gap of 1.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.2%.

A close pass involved a bus at 42.7 km/h with a gap of 1.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.8%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and protect people crossing.

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

At 20 km/h the impact speed for that event would have been 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk.

At 20 km/h the impact speed for that event would have been 3.3 km/h with 0.1% adult death risk.

Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety at North Avenue crossing

We are writing to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school.

Measurements from a Crossing Watch survey over 6.9 minutes (414.0 s) recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.5 km/h. A young pupil hit by the fastest vehicle would probably not have survived.

In that short period there was 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

The most serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s and involved a car at 16.9 km/h.

A separate close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s and involved a motorcycle at 44.4 km/h.

A separate close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s and involved a bus at 17.6 km/h.

Engineering context carries caveats: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 6.9 minutes, and 81.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more (4 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 41.7 s) with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request that the road authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect children crossing.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
