To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

Our school arranged a video measurement at North Avenue crossing for 3.7 minutes (222.0 s).

In that recording 12 pedestrian crossings and 41 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 61.3 km/h. 6 of 12 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 21.1-78.9% and 9.9-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Serious near-misses were defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. The video captured 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

The worst incidents were as follows. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car at 58.3 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 16.1%. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with a car at 23.2 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.8%. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s with an auto-rickshaw at 16.5 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.4%. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s with a car at 12.6 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.3%. One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a bus at 35.7 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 2.4%. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front per Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

For context, 83.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more, 0 of them 12 s or more and longest gap 10.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 3.7 minutes, so counts are limited to 12 pedestrian crossings and 41 moving vehicles.

We request a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h speed table and warning signs at this location to lower approach speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We can share the video and measurement data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Quarry Road crossing

We measured safety at the Quarry Road crossing using a video of 18.9 minutes covering 6 crossings and 21 vehicles. During this recording, 3 of 6 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 6 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 11.8-88.2% and 0.4-64.1% of crossings and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long. The 85th percentile speed was 49.6 km/h.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second near-miss was a close pass with a gap of 1.6 s involving an auto-rickshaw. The auto-rickshaw in that pass was travelling at 47.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 47.5 km/h the estimated death risk is 5.4%.

A third near-miss was a close pass with a gap of 2.3 s involving a car. The car in that pass was travelling at 34.1 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 19 pedestrians and 67 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 18.9 minutes of video, though a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also, 67.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, based on 4 gaps, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to slow vehicles and give priority to people crossing.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone with signs at this location. We are willing to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority, In 26.6 minutes (1596.0 s) of video at the Park Avenue crossing, Crossing Watch recorded 23 crossings and 10 vehicles, with 85th speed 66.3 km/h. 5 of 23 crossings (1 in 4.6) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 23 crossings (1 in 7.7) within 1.5 s. The 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 7.5-43.7% and 2.8-33.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), or 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses under 1.5 s and 2 close passes at 1.5-3.0 s, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart for serious and 1.5-3.0 s for close pass. 3 were person first and 1 was vehicle first and 1 was both at once. An additional serious case involved a car through the same spot 1.0 s from the person at 54.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front in that event the death risk was 12.3% (Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). The closest event was a car through the same spot 0.0 s from the person at 56.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front in that event the death risk was 14.0%, falling to 0.6% at impact 20.0 km/h under a 20.0 km/h limit. A further serious event was a bus through the same spot 1.4 s from the person at 38.9 km/h. A close pass was a bus through the same spot 2.3 s from the person at 58.4 km/h. A close pass was a car through the same spot 1.8 s from the person at 13.6 km/h. Scaled PV2 was 0.0 x 10^8 from 52 pedestrians and 23 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.6 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 65.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 42.5 s, with the first and last cut short by the video. Please install a raised zebra crossing at this crossing. We will share the video on request. Yours faithfully, The Principal

A close pass was 2.2 s apart with an auto-rickshaw at 15.3 km/h, carrying 0.0% adult death risk if hit by a car front, compared with 0.0% at 0.0 km/h impact.

A close pass was 2.9 s apart with a car at 20.8 km/h, carrying 0.0% adult death risk if hit by a car front, compared with 0.0% at 0.0 km/h impact.

57.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, but PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 5.9.

We request a raised zebra crossing at School Lane crossing and offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Canal Road crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch video for 6.6 minutes (396.0 s) recorded 4 pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 41.0 km/h.

The closest serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.1 s with a car at 34.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). We request a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We can share the video and measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write on behalf of our school about the crossing outside it on Hill View Road crossing. Yours faithfully,

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

On behalf of our school, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at the Ring Road crossing.

A video survey using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time recorded 3 pedestrian crossings and 3 moving vehicles over 4.1 minutes (246.0 s). In that time, 1 of 3 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 0 of 3 within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 0.8-90.6% and 0.0-70.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.0-5.6 and 0.0-3.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 0 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot 1.5-3.0 s apart.

The worst recorded event was a close pass with a 1.8 s gap involving a car. The vehicle speed was 12.7 km/h. This change is certain to save lives at this crossing. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.

The 85th percentile speed was 18.5 km/h. We note that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 4.1 minutes with 3 pedestrian crossings and 3 moving vehicles counted. Also, 86.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, including 10 gaps of 6 s or more and 7 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 51.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We therefore request a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority at the crossing point. We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,

The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We represent the school beside the Station Road crossing and ask for a raised zebra crossing with speed table.

We analysed video of the crossing totalling 1.5 minutes (90.0 s). In that time we counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 3 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.5 km/h. If this recording is typical, the exact 95% ranges are 2.8-60.0% and 0.3-48.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.2-7.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most serious event was a serious near-miss with 0.2 s between the person and a car travelling at 30.8 km/h. If hit as an adult by a car front the estimated death risk is 1.6%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h at a 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A separate close pass left 1.7 s between the person and a car at 50.5 km/h. If hit as an adult by a car front the estimated death risk is 5.6%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h at a 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Interpretation requires caution. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 1.5. In the available 1.5 minutes, 76.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more and 0 gaps of 12 s or more, longest 11.3 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. The UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds, while other groups such as children may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request that the road authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location and are happy to share the video for review. I can't create a plausible but unsupported claim for the letter, as that would introduce information the measurements do not support into a safety-related document.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
